criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Primary mission (reef monitoring via fluid lensing), rationale, single-spacecraft justification, and users/operator/funding all addressed with reasonable detail and references. Could be deeper on customer definition.

evidence.quote: Coral reefs, specifically the Great Barrier Reef, would immensely benefit from dedicated satellite monitoring.
Thus, only one satellite is required.
The proposed satellite would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM)

criteria.name: Main body: mission design - Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate - Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix) - Include the following information: • Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? • What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? • Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? • Which ground control facilities will you use? • How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? • How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: All major requirements addressed: launch site/vehicle with rationale, SSO with full COEs, manoeuvres (EOL only), ground station, access durations, 5-year mission and drag-sail EOL. STK screenshots and access reports included. Weaknesses: no software files mentioned, no hand-calculation derivations shown, error claiming low resolution 'is also desirable', Vega E not yet flown risk acknowledged only in conclusion.

criteria.reasoning: Conclusions summarise each segment and note risks (Vega E availability), but remain largely a restatement of the design rather than critical evaluation of results (e.g. access adequacy, coverage trade-offs).

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear structure with headings and TOC; figures have captions but are inconsistently labelled (no figure numbers). References are bare URLs with no titles/dates, and Wikipedia is cited, which is disallowed. Minor grammar errors ('is current owned', stray parenthesis).

technical_issues.issue: States low resolution from high altitude 'is also desirable' – contradicts resolution requirement for reef imaging.
Wikipedia cited as source [6], explicitly disallowed; references are bare URLs without titles/access dates.
Text garbled/contradictory: 'without thrusters... choose an uncontrolled descent... However, the ZYZZsat is without thrust capability' – repetitive and unclear; drag sail description incomplete.
Inclination-vs-altitude plot presented without showing the underlying J2 hand calculation or equation.
Claim that vertical inclination 'maintains a significant contact for the vast majority of passes' is vague and unsupported.

overall: A well-structured, mostly complete mission design for GBR reef monitoring with STK evidence and sound orbit/launch choices. Weakened by missing software files and hand-calculation detail, Wikipedia citation, bare-URL references, inconsistent figure labelling, and some garbled/erroneous passages.

feedback.summary: A well-structured, mostly complete mission design for GBR reef monitoring with good STK evidence and sound orbit/launch choices. To reach the top band: remove the Wikipedia citation and fix bare-URL references, show your hand calculations (e.g. J2 inclination), include software files, label figures consistently, and clarify the garbled EOL and resolution passages.
next_steps: Replace the Wikipedia source [6] with a citable primary source, and format all references with titles, authors and access dates so in-text citations match the list
Show the J2 hand calculation (equation and working) behind your inclination-vs-altitude plot, and attach your STK scenario/software files in an appendix

Rewrite the Mission Duration & EOL section to resolve the contradictory 'without thrusters' statements and fully describe the drag sail deorbit plan; also correct the claim that low resolution 'is also desirable' for reef imaging

criteria.C1: Strong work: your Introduction clearly covers the primary mission (fluid-lensing reef monitoring), why it is needed, the single-spacecraft justification, and users/operator/funding (CSIRO, BOM). To reach the top of the Accomplished band, deepen the customer definition - e.g. how reef managers would actually access and use the imagery.
criteria.C2: All major requirements are addressed with good STK screenshots and access reports, and your SSO/launch rationale is sound. The next level requires higher-quality supporting evidence: include software files, show hand-calculation derivations (e.g. the J2 inclination result), fix the low-resolution contradiction, and discuss the Vega E availability risk in the design body, not just the conclusion.
criteria.C3: Your conclusion summarises each segment and flags the Vega E risk, which is good. To move to Accomplished, go beyond restatement: critically evaluate results - is the achieved access duration adequate for the reef-monitoring requirement? What coverage or orbit trade-offs would you revisit?
criteria.C4: Clear structure with headings and TOC, and figures have captions. For Accomplished: add consistent figure numbers (Figure 1, 2...) referenced in text, replace bare-URL references with properly formatted citations (no Wikipedia), and proofread for errors like 'is current owned' and stray parentheses.
